interface.name: hyprglass_item_manager_v1

description.summary: manager to associate glass item hints with surfaces

interface.description:
This is a Hyprland-hyprglass-specific extension. It lets a client hint how the hyprglass compositor plugin should render the Liquid Glass effect it already applies to any surface that also carries an ext-background-effect-v1 blur region: which named preset to use, and what rounded-rect shape to clip the effect to.
This protocol only ever provides hints. A compositor without the hyprglass plugin loaded, or one that unloads it, has no obligation to honor any request here, and every object created by this protocol keeps working (as a silent no-op) rather than becoming a protocol error, precisely so that hint state never has to be treated as load-bearing by a client.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by bumping the major version of the extension.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This does not affect any hyprglass_item_v1 objects already created.

request.name: get_item

description.summary: create a glass item hint object for a surface

request.description:
Create a hyprglass_item_v1 object for the given wl_surface. Only one active (non-inert) such object may exist per surface at a time; creating a second one for the same surface while the first is still active raises the item_exists error. Inert objects left over from a previous manager global do not count.
This request does not, by itself, cause the surface to receive any glass effect: the effect is still gated on the surface itself carrying an ext-background-effect-v1 blur region. The object created here only supplies hints used when that effect is drawn.

event.name: finished
event.description:
Sent when the compositor is about to make this global permanently unusable, for example because the hyprglass plugin is being unloaded. The client should stop issuing new requests on this manager and any hyprglass_item_v1 objects it created; it does not have to destroy them, since they are guaranteed to remain valid, inert objects (see hyprglass_item_v1's own description) rather than become protocol errors.
This event is a courtesy for well-behaved clients and does not by itself guarantee no request already in flight will be silently dropped; that guarantee comes from every hyprglass_item_v1 request being defined as a no-op once the object is inert, regardless of this event's timing.

entry.name: item_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a hyprglass_item_v1 object

interface.name: hyprglass_item_v1

description.summary: glass rendering hints for one surface

interface.description:
Carries optional per-surface hints for the hyprglass Liquid Glass effect: which preset to use, and what rounded-rect shape to clip the effect to. The two hints are independent: either can be set without the other. None of these requests raises an error for an out-of-range value; being hints, invalid values are ignored or clamped as described per request. All state is double-buffered per wl_surface.commit, in the same manner as wp_viewport or ext_background_effect_surface_v1's set_blur_region: a request sets pending state, and it has no visible effect until the associated wl_surface.commit. For a synchronized wl_subsurface, "the associated commit" is the commit that applies that subsurface's cached state (i.e. its own commit if desynchronized, or the ancestor commit that flushes it if synchronized) — the same cached-state timing defined by wl_subsurface, not the raw wl_surface.commit request on this surface alone.
Once the hyprglass_item_manager_v1 global that created this object disappears (for example because the hyprglass plugin was unloaded), this object becomes inert: every request on it is silently ignored (no protocol error, no event, no effect on the surface), and the client is not disconnected. A client that keeps a reference to an inert object may destroy it at any time; it may also simply stop using it. Requests are inert independently per object — the disappearance of the manager global does not retroactively affect surfaces' rendering in any other way.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying this object clears the surface's association with it, but per the double-buffering rule above, any pending (uncommitted) state is simply discarded, and any state already latched by a previous commit is cleared on the next wl_surface.commit, mirroring ext_background_effect_surface_v1's own destroy semantics. If the wl_surface has already been destroyed, cleanup happens immediately.

request.name: set_preset

description.summary: hint which named preset to use

request.description: Sets the pending preset name. An empty string, or a name the hyprglass configuration does not recognize, is treated the same as unset_preset: the compositor falls back to its normal preset resolution chain for this surface (namespace/window default, then global default). The dark or light variant of the preset is still chosen by the parent window's theme, exactly as without this hint.

request.name: unset_preset
request.description: Reverts to the compositor's normal preset resolution chain, as if set_preset had never been called.

request.name: set_shape

description.summary: hint an explicit rounded-rect clip shape

request.description:
Sets the pending shape: a rectangle in surface-local logical coordinates, with up to four independent corner radii, that the glass effect is clipped and shaped to. x/y may be negative and/or w/h may extend past the surface's own extents — for example, an item whose top edge is cropped by a wp_viewport when scrolled can report its full, uncropped logical shape here; the ext-background-effect-v1 blur region set on the surface (or an ancestor) is still applied as a flat clip on top of this shape and is the final word on which pixels ever show the effect.
If w or h is zero or negative, the shape is ignored and the pending state behaves as after unset_shape (a transient layout state such as a collapsing menu is not an error). A negative radius is treated as zero. Radii are not required to fit within w/h — an oversized radius is clamped the same way a CSS border-radius would be (each pair of radii sharing an edge is scaled down proportionally so they no longer overlap). Corners are circular arcs.
Calling this request after set_inherit_shape (in the same or an earlier pending state) makes this shape take effect instead; set_shape and set_inherit_shape are mutually exclusive, and whichever was requested most recently in the pending state wins.

request.name: set_inherit_shape

description.summary: hint to reuse the parent window's shape

request.description:
Requests that the item be shaped by the parent window's own rounded box: the window's geometry, corner rounding and rounding_power (its squircle exponent), instead of an explicit shape. The blur region still clips it flat. An edge-attached item (e.g. a full-width bar at the bottom of the window) therefore gets the window's corners on the window edges it touches and straight edges elsewhere, and a full-window scrim follows the window outline without its region having to match it exactly. This is a distinct request, not a magic radius value passed to set_shape, since rounding_power is not expressible as a radius.
This is mutually exclusive with set_shape; whichever of the two was requested most recently in the pending state wins. It has no effect if the surface has no associated window (for example, a layer-shell or standalone surface).

request.name: unset_shape
request.description: Reverts to the compositor's normal shape fallback for an item with no explicit shape, as if set_shape and set_inherit_shape had never been called: the extents of its ext-background-effect-v1 blur region, with corners from the plugin:hyprglass:subsurfaces:radius setting (a capsule by default).
